note: The Moose easter eggs, in one place so they are easy to audit and to add to each season. None of them changes a number or a rule: the rule book and the values in tables stay authoritative. Read by site/eggs.py.
antlers: Wherever the team appears in a table, an antler fades in above the name on hover.
title_watermark: The champion banner carries a moose watermark in the team's title seasons, whichever they are.

rivalry_captions.best: America's Team owns this one: {team} lead the series {w}-{l}.
rivalry_captions.losing: In fairness, {opp} have the Moose's number: {l}-{w} against them.

not_found.title: This page has been retained by the Moose
not_found.text: Whatever was here cost three retainment slots, and the Moose paid them.

museum.title: America's Team
museum.text: A franchise museum. There is no link to it, and the Moose would like it kept that way.

konami: Up up down down left right left right B A: the accent turns moose brown, the moose runs across the screen, and for a moment every team in the standings is the Moose. Picking the Moose in the trades page's team filter does the same. Arriving at the Moose's franchise page does too.

barney.what: Typing barney on any page turns the site purple, pops up F-Jackie's Barney logo for a few seconds, and renames F-Jackie to Barney in every table until he leaves. Script: site/assets/barney.js. The image is F-Jackie's MFL logo since 2019, from the original site's images/logos. Picking F-Jackie in the trades page's team filter calls him too. He also pops up on arrival at F-Jackie's franchise page.
barney.hint: Someone purple is never far away. Try typing his name.

clips.what: An inflatable tube man slides up in the corner and flails. Made from a GIF the commissioner supplied in 2026.
A rider on an electric scooter between two beer steins: don't drink and drive. Made from a GIF the commissioner supplied in 2026.
A bearded man studies his pint. Made from a GIF the commissioner supplied in 2026.

Travis Henry's infamous halfback pass, Dolphins at Bills, September 21, 2003, embedded from the Buffalo Archives Now YouTube channel rather than copied, and starting muted in YouTube's own player, which takes clicks for play and sound, and stays until its close button is pressed. If the upload is taken down, the egg shows an empty player: drop this entry. The caption is the league's reason for it: the OakalDoakals took Henry 1st overall in 2007, ahead of the three picks after him, all from the draft data.
clips.caption:
{overall} overall, {year}: {pick}. The next three picks: {next}, all three fantasy studs.
In his honor, Travis Henry at quarterback.

clips.what: A green army man throws his red cup: go commando. Made from a GIF the commissioner supplied in 2026, set on white because the GIF's background is transparent.

clips.caption: Playoffs? Bunchalosers made them {playoffs} times in {seasons} seasons. Sound on for Jim Mora.
clips.what: Jim Mora's playoffs press conference (Colts, 2001), embedded from the Inside the 49ers YouTube channel, under a caption with the team's playoff trips from the record. The joke is the audio, which browsers will not autoplay, so the caption asks for sound. Stays until closed.

clips_note: Arriving at each team's franchise page, its clip slides up in the corner and plays for the seconds given (a click sends it off, and 0 keeps it until closed). Script: site/assets/clip.js, loaded on those pages only. Each clip is site/assets/<clip>.mp4, re-encoded from the GIF, with <clip>.jpg as its still for reduced motion. An entry with "youtube" (a video id) embeds that video instead, and "clip" is only the player's title.

magazine.what: Arriving at the Karpet Munchers' franchise page, a glossy draft-guide magazine slides up in the corner. Its can't-miss sleepers are their own four worst early picks (rounds 1 and 2, 2008 on, by starts under what the slot usually yields), and a sticky note gives the starts. Built by eggs.magazine(), shown by site/assets/clip.js. A click closes it. The cover line and the Leshoure line on the note are the league's own story of the 2011 pick (5th overall, A.J. Green 6th, per the draft data). Two heckles are stuck on it, from the Pounders and the Otters, the trade count from the record.
magazine.note_extra: Leshoure went one pick ahead of A.J. Green, with a torn Achilles.

heckles.text: {trades} trades in {seasons} years. Do you own a phone?
Leshoure over A.J. Green. We'll never forget.

outage.what: Arriving at the Texas Nashvillians' franchise page, the page flickers and switches off like an old television, an outage notice comes up, and a bucket truck drives in, raises its boom to the pole and restores the power. About seven seconds, and a click restores it at once. Reduced motion gets the notice alone, briefly. Script: site/assets/outage.js.

trade_offer.what: Arriving at Couchfire's franchise page, a trade proposal comes up. Decline runs from the pointer three times before it gives in, Accept is already too late, and however it ends, the couch-on-fire clip plays (site/assets/couch-fire.mp4, from a GIF the commissioner supplied in 2026). Script: site/assets/trade.js. Its words are below.
get: A tight end who retired in 2019
trade_offer.note: Trust me, this helps both of us.
trade_offer.accepted: Too late. Couchfire already made this trade in one of his other 19 leagues.
trade_offer.declined: Declined. Couchfire has countered: the same trade, plus his backup kicker.

grumpy_train.what: Arriving at Ho Train's franchise page, a scowling steam engine chugs in from the right, stops mid-screen to grumble one line at random, and chugs off to the left (a click sends it away). Two lines come from the record: the best finished season and, while one is in progress, this season. Script: site/assets/train.js, the engine drawn for the site.
lines: Your lineup is wrong. I didn't look. I can tell.
The rules change every year. I hated all of them.
grumpy_train.best: Back in {year} we went {record} and nobody made a fuss.
grumpy_train.now: {record} this season. Don't talk to me.

build_log.what: Once Moose mode has run on the Moose's franchise page, a terminal slides up in the corner and types out the commissioner's site build, its counts from the record, the rule book's ledger and the built site. It closes itself after, or with its button. Script: site/assets/commish.js. A line starting "$ " is typed out, and a "|" is a pause. Schedule luck comes from the luck table on the franchise pages: while another team has had more, the log names it and protests, and once the Moose lead, it credits skill instead. The trade lines count trades the record marks as processed by the commissioner, the Moose's against everyone else's.
lines: Computing all-play, luck and standard deviations nobody asked for...| done
Checking the rule book for bias toward the Moose...| 0 found
Reclassifying them as Super Bowl appearances...| done
Reviewing {trades} Moose trades for fairness...| {by_commish} processed by the commissioner ({mine_rate}%)
Same rate for everyone else's trades...| {others_rate}%
Writing {pages} pages nobody will read...| done
WARNING: commissioner has not gone outside since August
luck_lines: Computing schedule luck...| {luck} wins, {luck_rank} in the league
Filing a protest with the commissioner...| denied
luck_first_lines: Computing schedule luck...| {luck} wins, the most in the league

y2k.what: A moment after arriving at the Dunbar Dogs' franchise page, it turns into a home page from 2000: gray, Times New Roman, blue underlined links, a scrolling marquee, an under-construction banner, a hit counter and a news box. The news comes from the rule book's ledger (the divisions drawn from a hat, then restored) and the team's draft picks. A button brings 2026 back. Script: site/assets/y2k.js, built by eggs.y2k().
y2k.marquee: *** RESTORE THE ORIGINAL DIVISIONS *** WELCOME TO THE DUNBAR DOGS HOME PAGE *** NO RULE CHANGES PLEASE *** SIGN MY GUESTBOOK ***
news: {restored}: The ORIGINAL DIVISIONS are RESTORED!!! (After {hat_seasons} seasons of drawing them out of a hat.)
Rule changes since 2000: {changes}. Rule changes the {team} wanted: 0.
Wide receivers drafted: {wr} ({wr_pct}% of our picks). Running backs are a fad.
y2k.footer: Best viewed in Netscape Navigator 4.0 at 800x600. Guestbook coming soon! Last updated: August 2000.

tank.what: On the Tally Wackers' franchise page, while the tube man flails, a tank flying a SUCK FOR LUCK flag rolls in, stops under a report card on the season before they took Andrew Luck 1st overall (record, points against the next-lowest team, his starts in his first three seasons, titles since, all from the record), then charges a brick wall at the right edge, bounces off it and catches fire. Once the tank has gone, their sign-in sheet for the draft and summer meeting slides up: present in the years below, absent in every other. The attendance is the league's lore, not a record. Scripts: site/assets/tank.js and clip.js.
tank.title: {year} report card

beers.what: On Beers' franchise page, while the beer clip plays, dozens of messy legal-pad pages flutter down and land in a heap: one on every franchise Beers have traded with (the trade counts from the record, the scrawl below) and a few more, and on top the switchboard, Beers in the middle with a line to every franchise as thick as their trades. A click, Escape or 20 seconds sweeps them away. Once the clip has gone, the rumor mill crawls along the bottom: every rumor is made up, and says so by being absurd. Scripts: site/assets/notes.js and rumor.js.
beers.label: Beers hears
rumors: {top} and Beers are talking again. That would be trade {top_next}.
Couchfire has sent the same trade offer to 19 other leagues.
Karpet Munchers have pre-ordered next summer's draft magazine.
Ho Train says he is not grumpy. Ho Train is grumpy.
Dunbar Dogs have filed a protest against the year 2001.
Tally Wackers will attend the next meeting. Source: none.
A Manic Moose trade was approved in record time. By the commissioner.
OakalDoakals are drawing up a halfback pass.
Scooter's Boozers have arranged a ride home.
Otters are growing moustaches for the playoffs.
Texas Nashvillians would like everyone to stop emailing.
Beers have made {total} trades. Second place has {next_most}.
Beers would like a word about your 2027 1st.

relabel.what: On the Moose's own franchise page, the Super Bowl losses fact is labelled with "Super Bowl losses" struck through and "Super Bowl appearances" after it. The years listed are the same.

iron_city.what: On the Iron City Pounders' franchise page, a typed parish-bulletin program for the Autumn Bowl (St. Sebastian's vs. St. Bonaventure's) slides up on arrival, and a plaque hangs under the team's name for good: its longest-kept player from the archived rosters (2003 on), the runner-up on its own roster, and its trades over that run. eggs.autumn() and eggs.plaque(); the program is shown by site/assets/clip.js.

program.title: THE AUTUMN BOWL
details: Please do not park on the rectory lawn.
program.featuring: FEATURING the {team}, who will now tell you about it. Again.

plaque_lines: Trades in that time: {trades}. Seasons without one: {quiet}.
iron_city.plaque_hint: From the archived MFL rosters, end of each season, 2003 on.

rx.what: On F-Jackie's franchise page, once Barney has gone, a doctor's prescription slides up. The diagnosis is the team's schedule luck from the luck table the franchise pages use (the worst in the league, and by how much), and the second opinion is the Texas Nashvillians'. eggs.rx(), shown by site/assets/clip.js.
lines: Diagnosis: chronic bad luck. {luck} wins against what the scoring was worth, {rank} ({other_label}: {other}, {other_luck}).
rx.script: Take two Barneys and call me in the morning.
rx.second: Second opinion, Texas Nashvillians: “The dumbest doctor I know.”

page_heckles.text: I can't believe the Tally Wackers have made the playoffs 19 times and have never won a championship. That might be more impressive than actually winning every now and then. Is Tomlin coaching them?
page_heckles.check: Record check: {playoffs} playoff trips, {finals} Super Bowls, {titles} titles. The most playoff trips without a title by anyone else: {next_team}, {next_playoffs}.

page_heckles.text: He's gotten better at not making bad trade offers.
At least the Tally Wackers were sucking for Luck. F-Jackie is just sucking to suck.
page_heckles.check: Record check: {record_now} in {season}, {rank_now} of {teams}. On October 11, Josh Allen went to the Texas Nashvillians for Joe Burrow, Jonah Coleman and a 2028 1st, and Burrow went straight on to Couchfire the same day for J.J. McCarthy and a 2027 1st. Net: Josh Allen became J.J. McCarthy, Jonah Coleman and two 1sts.

page_heckles_note: Quotes from other teams, pinned under a franchise's facts on its page for good, each with a check from the record beneath it. eggs.page_heckle(). A quote without a "check" has none (trade offers, for one, are not in the record).

draft_grade.what: On Scooter's Boozers' franchise page, once the clip has gone, a draft report card slides up: A+, graded by the team two minutes after the draft. Four seconds later the A+ is struck out and REVISED stamped over it, with the record's numbers: the share of picks that became starters (finished drafts, 2008 on, as the franchise pages count it), the league's, and both since 2016. eggs.draft_grade(), shown by site/assets/clip.js.
draft_grade.title: Draft report card
meta: Time since the draft ended: 2 minutes

out_of_office.what: On F-Jackie's franchise page, an email notification slides in at the top right: an automatic reply from Buddy, the team's former co-manager, who did the work until he left. The rule book's changes are counted from its ledger. eggs.out_of_office(), shown by site/assets/clip.js. The commissioner chose to name him.
out_of_office.subject: Automatic reply: Re: {team}
body: For questions about lineups, waivers or the rules, please contact the remaining owner, who will not know.
out_of_office.rules: The {link} is here: {changes} changes since 2000. I read all of them. So that one of us had.

texts.what: On Blitzkrieg's franchise page, a phone thread slides up: texts from other teams arrive one at a time, every one delivered and none answered (the trade counts in them are each sender's trades with Blitzkrieg, from the record), Blitzkrieg starts typing and gives up, and the last line is its latest title. eggs.texts(), shown by site/assets/clip.js.

messages.text: We've traded {n} times. Wanna make it {next}?
Sent you an offer. Also sent it to 19 other leagues.

towels.what: On Da Funk's franchise page, a row of waving yellow towels rises along the bottom with one Dolphins flag in the middle. The sign above it compares the league's most Steelers-heavy rosters with Da Funk's Dolphins share (end-of-season rosters from 2003 on, players only) and lists the Dolphins it drafted (a pick counts if the player was on Miami's roster that season, by the archived MFL player list). eggs.towels(), shown by site/assets/clip.js.
towels.title: The only Dolphins fan in Pittsburgh
lines: {team} rosters: {mia}% Dolphins, {mia_rank} in the league. {above} have rostered more Dolphins than the Dolphins fan.
Dolphins drafted (on Miami's roster that season): {fins}.

funk_chat.what: On Da Funk's franchise page, a league chat window opens at the top right: Da Funk enters, starts typing, thinks better of it and leaves. Underneath, its waiver adds a season (and where that ranks) and trades a season, from the activity tables. eggs.funk_chat(), shown by site/assets/clip.js.
funk_chat.foot: {adds} waiver adds a season, the {adds_rank} fewest in the league. {trades} trades a season.

champagne.what: On Da Funk's franchise page, once the towels have gone, a champagne bottle on ice slides up, in the manner of the 1972 Dolphins' bottle for the day the last unbeaten team loses. While Da Funk is unbeaten this season the bottle is reserved for it, otherwise it goes back in the fridge. Then its regular-season winning run if it is six or more (and whether it is the league's longest), the playoff record, the #1-seed exits, who knocked it out most and the seasons it led the league in points and still went out, all from the playoff brackets. eggs.champagne(), shown by site/assets/clip.js.
champagne.title: ON ICE

unbeaten.intro: The 1972 Dolphins keep a bottle on ice for the day the last unbeaten team loses. This one is for {team}.

beaten.intro: The cork stays in: {team} is {w}-{l}. Maybe next year.

lines: Led the league in points in {led} and went out in the playoffs anyway.
champagne.close: The 1972 Dolphins also won their playoff games.
champagne.streak: {streak} regular-season wins in a row, the longest run in league history.

scoreboard.what: On Carter's Commandos' franchise page, once the clip has gone, a stadium scoreboard flips between two finals: its lowest-scoring title game and its highest-scoring playoff loss (and says so if no team has scored more in a playoff loss). Below, the season it ranked highest in points and still missed the playoffs, with its schedule luck and where that ranks among every season. eggs.scoreboard(), shown by site/assets/clip.js.
scoreboard.title: SCOREBOARD
scoreboard.headline: Explain that.
lines: {title_score} points won a title in {title_season}. {loss_score} lost a playoff game in {loss_season}.
And {bad}: {bad_rank} in points, {bad_record}, no playoffs. The {luck_rank} unluckiest season on record ({luck} wins).
scoreboard.record: No team has ever scored more in a playoff loss.

giant_killer.what: On Carter's Commandos' franchise page, a small gold trophy sits under the title for good: every playoff win over a #1 seed as a lower seed, from the playoff brackets. eggs.giant_killer().
giant_killer.title: GIANT KILLER
giant_killer.line: Beat the #1 seed in {season} as the {seed}-seed. Victim: {opp}, {me}-{them}.

steeler_board.what: On Carter's Commandos' franchise page, after the scoreboard, its first-round draft board: Steelers circled (the player's NFL team that season, by the archived MFL player list), first-rounders with one start or fewer crossed out (finished drafts only), and the team's Steelers share of roster spots with its rank. eggs.steeler_board(), shown by site/assets/clip.js.
steeler_board.title: War room: round 1
steeler_board.key: Circled: Steelers. Crossed out: first-rounders with one start or fewer.
steeler_board.foot: Steelers: {pit}% of the team's roster spots since 2003, {pit_rank} in the league.

otter.label: Waiver adds
otter.what: On the Otters' franchise page, an otter floats on its back across the bottom of the screen with a waiver claim on its belly, under a bubble counting up its waiver adds (and saying so if no team has made more), its draft hit rate's rank from the bottom and its top-3 finishes in points (finished seasons). eggs.otter(), shown by site/assets/otter.js. It replaced the moustached-otters clip, a first attempt.

released.what: On the Otters' franchise page, a transaction notice slides in at the top right: the player they dropped who scored the most for other teams afterwards, from the got-away table, stamped RELEASED. eggs.released(), shown by site/assets/clip.js.
released.head: Transaction

vhs.what: On the Otters' franchise page, once the otter has floated off, a VHS tape slides up: their December highlights, from the playoff record. The lowest score in a final they lost, the costliest playoff benching, the closest playoff loss (and whether the winner took the title) and the most points given up in one. The label counts the titles, not shown. eggs.vhs(), shown by site/assets/clip.js.
vhs.title: {team}: DECEMBER HIGHLIGHTS
vhs.bench: {season}: lost to {opp} by {by}, with {bench} points on the bench.
vhs.close_champ: {opp} went on to win the title.

fact_check.what: On the Otters' franchise page, a fact-check sticky note under the title for good: their all-time series with the Karpet Munchers, whom they like to mock, and the playoff meetings, which the Munchers lead. eggs.fact_check().
fact_check.title: FACT CHECK
fact_check.hint: From head to head and the playoff brackets
